name: cz-harness
description: An AI-native delivery Harness for FPT project managers. RD-driven, fully traceable, real-time observable. Ships as a Claude Code plugin: 10 role subagents, 22 slash commands, 7 packaged skills, 9 enforcing hooks + 1 cosmetic deliverable-rendering hook, 3 gate profiles, an event-sourced live board, and an HTML-rendered deliverables system for every agent's output (see docs/DELIVERABLES.md).
buildPhase: 0-5 scaffold — see docs/ and §12 of the plan for exit criteria not yet exercised against a real runtime
notes: 1.0.22: new command, requested after a manual real-project audit (AI-bootcamp, 41 RDs) applying the 7 traceability-integrity dimensions from the plan's own governance framing (coverage, change coupling, freshness, orphan rate, review evidence, decision coverage, retrieval quality — the same 7 named in docs/PILLAR-MAP.md's Governance pillar and skills/traceability/SKILL.md's framing, not a new taxonomy) found real gaps that neither existing command surfaces: two REQs (parent_req targets of an entire RD lineage that went 002.01-style superseded/withdrawn with no live successor) read as "has RDs" to any pure graph check, since /cz:report's RTM orphan-class-1 only asks whether a RD exists for a REQ, not whether any RD of it is still alive; separately, every gate-records/*.json in that project had gate_decision.approver:"auto" with zero literal human-sign-off traces, and test files cited RD ids that had since gone withdrawn, both real but invisible to /cz:audit (which checks telemetry/board replay-consistency, not documentation quality) and to /cz:report (which requires an approved gate to run at all, so it can't be used as an early health read). New commands/cz-health-check.md fills that gap: read-only, no gate, safe to run at any project stage (unlike /cz:report), scores the 7 dimensions from real file/telemetry evidence and writes deliverables/HEALTH-CHECK-<code>.md via agentops (new Write(deliverables/HEALTH-CHECK*.md) grant on agents/agentops.md, alongside its existing RTM/WEEKLY/CASE-STUDY scope) with step:n/a since it's cross-cutting, not tied to one of the 11 phases. Wired per docs/DELIVERABLES.md's own "Adding a new deliverable kind" checklist: HEALTH-CHECK added to the frontmatter kind enum and the deliverable-ownership table, agentops.md's responsibilities/hard-rule-3/deliverable-format sections updated, and docs/OPERATOR-GUIDE.md §6 gained an entry alongside /cz:audit and /cz:rebuild-state. Purely additive — no existing command, hook, schema, or gate behavior changed; command count 21 -> 22.

1.0.21: bugfix, user-reported with a screenshot of the 1.0.20 session-detail modal's main timeline showing only tool-call names (Bash, Read, Edit...) with no sign of what Claude actually said or did between them. Root cause: parseLogText only ever extracted assistant `tool_use` content blocks into toolCalls/runs — the assistant's own `text` reply blocks (its natural-language explanations, summaries, 'done, here's what I found') were parsed nowhere in the top-level dataset, only inside the new subagent-trajectory summarizer added in 1.0.20's merge script, which doesn't cover the main session thread at all. Fixed by adding a new dataset.assistantMessages array, populated in three places: parseLogText's assistant-content loop (new `else if (block.type==="text")` branch alongside the existing tool_use branch), generateMockDataset (new REPLY_SNIPPETS pool, ~50% chance per mock turn, so the sample/demo view exercises this too), and finalizeSessions' touch() calls (so a session's start/end bounds still account for these timestamps, defensively, even though they'll typically coincide with an already-touched usage event on the same line). openSessionModal now merges these into the timeline as a new 'reply' item kind — amber dot, 'Claude' label, same click-to-expand truncated-text pattern as prompts — interleaved chronologically with prompts/tool calls/agent-skill runs. Verified live: re-opened the exact session from the user's screenshot and confirmed 79 real reply items now appear (previously 0), with actual assistant text like 'The usage monitor server started and merged logs from 2 projects.' rendering inline between the tool calls that produced it. Dashboard-only, no data/gate/state changes; the merge script (serve-usage-monitor.sh) is untouched by this fix.

1.0.20: major feature, user-requested ("a clear view/history of a session to help analysis or trace back what went wrong, click on each session opens a modal") — following up on a research question about whether Claude Code's default logs contain agent-trajectory data. Investigated real ~/.claude/projects/*/<sessionId>/ sidecar folders (not just the top-level *.jsonl the dashboard already parsed) and confirmed they hold each Task/Agent-spawned subagent's COMPLETE trajectory: subagents/agent-<hash>.jsonl (every thinking/tool_use/tool_result/text step, in order) plus agent-<hash>.meta.json (agentType, description, toolUseId linking back to the parent transcript's Task tool_use block, spawnDepth for nested sub-subagents) — contradicting 1.0.13's changelog claim that this sidecar data 'is not additional log data'. board/serve-usage-monitor.sh now also walks each session's subagents/ folder and writes merged/<project>.subagents.json (sessionId -> [{agentId, toolUseId, agentType, description, spawnDepth, steps}], steps capped at 4000/2000 chars per text/tool-input field to keep merge output bounded — 10MB for the AI-bootcamp project's 19 sessions with subagent activity); manifest.json entries gained a subagentsFile pointer, fetched best-effort alongside each project's main merged log in usage-monitor.html's auto-load block (silently absent under file:// or manual file-picker mode — this feature is auto-load-only, and the modal says so explicitly when trajectory data isn't available for a given run). New: sessionCell rows in both the Sessions table and the Agent & skill run log table are now clickable (row-clickable, click anywhere except the title's own expand-toggle) and open a session-detail modal — header (title/id/project/entrypoint), a stat strip (duration, started, prompts, tokens, cache hit, peak context, idle rate, reusing existing computations), and a chronological timeline merging prompts, plain tool calls, and agent/skill runs; each agent/skill run with matched subagent data (via run.toolUseId, newly captured in parseLogText's pendingRuns) is click-expandable to show its full nested trajectory (thinking italicized, tool_use with name+input, tool_result with error state highlighted). Caught and fixed a layout bug during verification: modal-body lacked flex:1/min-height:0 and .modal lacked overflow:hidden, so the header/stats scrolled away with the content instead of staying pinned — fixed before shipping. Verified live against real merged logs: a 14-prompt/6-subagent session rendered a 215-item timeline, one subagent expanded to its full 295-step trajectory (matching the source file's actual line count), and two of that session's agent runs correctly showed the 'trajectory detail not available' fallback (their subagent data legitimately wasn't captured, not a matching bug) — all three modal-close paths (X button, backdrop click, Escape) verified working.

1.0.19: bugfix, user-reported with a screenshot — board/usage-monitor.html's Cost estimator rate inputs (Sonnet/Opus/Haiku/Other IN and OUT $/MTOK fields) were rendering their digits clipped/overlapping (e.g. '15' showing as '1£', '0.8' showing as '0,') because the native input[type=number] spin-button (up/down stepper) arrows were overlapping the narrow field's text at the .rate-fields grid's width, with no room reserved for both. Fixed by disabling the native spinner (-webkit-appearance:none on ::-webkit-inner/outer-spin-button, -moz-appearance:textfield for Firefox) on the shared 'select, input[type=number]...' rule, plus min-width:0 + box-sizing:border-box so the fields size correctly inside their flex row. Verified live: all four rate cards now show their full unclipped values. Separately noted (not changed, flagged to user): Haiku's IN field displays '0,8' rather than '0.8' because Chrome renders type=number values using the OS locale's decimal separator — the underlying value is unaffected, this is a display-only locale quirk pre-existing before this fix, not something introduced by it. Dashboard-only, no data/gate/state changes.

1.0.18: board/usage-monitor.html's Sessions table gains a 'Cache read' column, user-requested ("can capture cached token for each session"). Per session this shows the raw cached-token count (fmtCompact) plus a cache hit-rate % underneath (cacheRead ÷ (cacheRead+tokensIn), where tokensIn already includes cache-creation tokens per the existing aggregation — i.e. hit rate = cache-served ÷ total input replayed that session), with the exact breakdown in the cell's hover title. No data-model change needed: s.cacheRead was already aggregated per session in both finalizeSessions() (real logs) and generateMockDataset() (mock data) for the top-level 'Cache reads' card, just not previously surfaced per-session. New cacheReadCell() helper, same two-line value+caption pattern as sessionCell()'s title/meta split. Verified against real merged logs (94-98% hit rates on the AI-bootcamp project's sessions, consistent with heavy prompt-cache reuse across a long-running agentic coding session) and against the mock/sample dataset (77-94% hit rates, no console errors on either path). Dashboard-only, no data/gate/state changes.

1.0.17: board/usage-monitor.html's Session overview gains a context-rot risk signal, user-requested ("can show info of % context usage in each session, to determine if the session has risk of context rot"). New CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS (200000, a stated assumption — the standard Claude context window, not read from any API since usage events don't carry the model's actual window size) and CONTEXT_RISK_WARN/HIGH (0.5/0.8) constants. Per session, peakContextTokens = the largest single assistant turn's (tokensIn + cacheRead + cacheCreate) — this approximates the full prompt replayed to the model that turn (fresh + cache-served + newly-cached), which is the best available proxy for how close a turn got to the context window, since raw cumulative token totals would conflate total spend with actual in-context size. Computed in both finalizeSessions() (real logs: max over every event in the session) and generateMockDataset() (mock data: the turn loop's per-turn baseIn was fresh-only rather than growing, which made every session read as equally low-risk regardless of length — an inert demo of a feature meant to differentiate sessions — so it now tracks a running convTokens the same way a real multi-turn conversation grows: each turn's cacheRead is the accumulated prior conversation, replayed from cache, mirroring how Claude Code actually resends history). New Sessions table column 'Peak context' renders a color-coded pill (green/amber/red at the same thresholds, reusing the existing .pill success/running/fail classes) with the exact peak-tokens-of-window in its hover title; two new stat tiles, 'Sessions at context risk' (count at or above the warn threshold) and 'Highest peak context' (the single riskiest turn in range, intentionally shown uncapped past 100% when a session's peak exceeds the assumed window, as a stronger signal rather than being silently clamped). Verified live: real merged logs show peak turns as high as 217% of the 200K assumption on some long sessions, 39 of 66 sessions flagged at-risk — plausible for long agentic coding sessions with large tool outputs in context, but the 200K figure is a heuristic default, not a per-model lookup, and is stated as such in the tile captions/tooltips so it doesn't read as an authoritative number. Dashboard-only, no data/gate/state changes.

1.0.16: board/usage-monitor.html session titles (Sessions table + Agent & skill run log table, both via the shared sessionCell() helper) are now click/keyboard-expandable instead of silently truncating. Previously sessionTitle() hard-truncated to 72 chars in JS, so even the native `title` hover tooltip only ever showed the same 72-char snippet — no way to read a long first-prompt title in full. Fixed by removing the JS-side truncation (sessionTitle() now returns the full derived text) and doing the visual truncation purely in CSS via -webkit-line-clamp:1 on .sess-title; a new click handler (also wired to Enter/Space via tabIndex=0 + role=button for keyboard/a11y) toggles a .expanded class that sets line-clamp:unset so the cell wraps and shows the complete text inline, no popup/modal needed. Dotted-underline + pointer cursor signal it's interactive; native title attribute retained as a hover fallback. Verified live: clicking a long first-prompt title (a 1300+ char session) expanded the row from ~20px to ~1300px and back on second click, with page-text confirming the full untruncated string is present. Dashboard-only, no data/gate/state changes.

1.0.15: board/usage-monitor.html's Session overview gains three new stat tiles — Agent run time, Idle time, Idle rate — plus more legible session identity throughout. Active/idle split is computed per session from inter-event gaps (all timestamped events/prompts/tool-calls, sorted): a new IDLE_GAP_MS constant (3 min) buckets each gap into 'agent run time' (<= threshold, sum of Math.min(gap, IDLE_GAP_MS)) or 'idle time' (overage beyond it, sum of Math.max(0, gap-IDLE_GAP_MS)); idle rate = idle / (idle + active). Implemented in both finalizeSessions() (real log parsing, tracks each session's full sorted timestamp array) and generateMockDataset() (mock/sample data, accumulated inline from the existing turn-gap loop) so the two data paths stay consistent. Separately, user-requested: the Session column on both the Sessions table and the Agent & skill run log table no longer shows a bare truncated session ID — new sessionTitle()/sessionCell()/buildSessionLookup() helpers derive a human title from the session's first prompt (slash-command invocations are unwrapped from their <command-message>/<command-name> XML envelope to just the command name, e.g. '/cz-harness:usage-monitor'; other XML-ish text has tags stripped; empty/unmatched sessions fall back to '<project-dir-name> · <entrypoint>', then finally 'Session <short-id>'), with the short session ID and project directory name shown as a subtitle underneath. Both tables now share this rendering path. No change to data collection, gates, or the board/state model — dashboard-only.

1.0.14: bugfix for 1.0.13's auto-load block — its own explanatory comment contained the literal path '~/.claude/projects/*/', whose trailing '*/' prematurely closed the enclosing JS block comment, turning the rest of the comment text into invalid JavaScript and throwing a SyntaxError that silently killed the whole app script (caught only by the page's own frame-runtime error reporter, so it surfaced as a generic 'Uncaught {stack:...}' console entry, not an obvious one). Auto-load, the project-filter dropdown, and even the base sample-data view were all broken as a result — this was caught live: the command reported success and the dropdown appeared to render in one check, but a fresh page load (cache-busted) reproduced the failure, confirming it wasn't transient. Fix: reworded the comment to remove the literal '*/' substring (now 'merges each ~/.claude/projects subfolder's session logs...'); verified with `node --check` against the extracted app <script> block, which now parses clean, and against a live reload showing 'All projects (2)' with 7,075 turns / 33.17M tokens auto-loaded. No functional/behavioral change from 1.0.13's intent — comment text only.

1.0.13: board/usage-monitor.html gains an optional auto-load block (no-op under file://, so opening it directly is unchanged — sample data + manual 'Load Claude log…' picker) that activates only when served over http(s): it fetch()es manifest.json + merged/*.jsonl next to itself, adds a project-filter dropdown to the topbar ('All projects (N)' or any single project), and renders real data immediately with no manual file picking. New board/serve-usage-monitor.sh is the local server that makes this activate: it merges every project's session logs under ~/.claude/projects/*/ into one manifest.json + one merged/<project>.jsonl per project inside ~/.claude/usage-monitor-run/ (top-level *.jsonl files only — each session's sidecar subfolder next to its .jsonl is not additional log data), copies the dashboard there as index.html, (re)starts a 127.0.0.1:8791 python3 http.server, and opens it. commands/usage-monitor.md now runs that script by default, falling back to the original plain file:// open of board/usage-monitor.html if the script is missing or fails. User-requested — they wanted every project's usage visible by just running the command, without manually merging *.jsonl files or clicking through the file picker each time, and asked for the ability to scope the view to a single project. board/usage-monitor.html's own picker-based, sample-data-by-default behavior is preserved byte-for-byte when opened directly; nothing about board/board.html or the cz-harness board/state model changed.

1.0.12: commands/usage-monitor.md now opens a plugin-bundled copy of the dashboard (board/usage-monitor.html, new file) instead of the claude.ai-hosted artifact URL. The dashboard was already a fully static, self-contained HTML/CSS/JS page — sample data by default, an in-page 'Load Claude log…' file picker reading local logs client-side via the browser File API, no fetch() calls, nothing uploaded — so it needed no adaptation to run standalone; it's opened directly as file:// (no local HTTP server, unlike board/board.html, since it has no ../state/board.json fetch to break under file://). This removes the command's dependency on claude.ai hosting/login/network access. The bundled copy is a manual snapshot, not a live mirror: if the hosted artifact at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/cce47a78-3918-4dc6-bbbb-32688a994f2b is edited and republished, board/usage-monitor.html must be re-copied by hand and the plugin version bumped again.

1.0.11: board/board.html gains the Deliverables and Audit & Outcomes tabs 1.0.10 said this plugin didn't ship — ported from the downstream project's own forked board.html referenced in that note, plus a new board/build-audit-index.py (builds gate-records/index.json: the audit trail and outcome/rework-rate metrics both tabs read, alongside deliverables/index.json which hooks/render-deliverable.sh already produces). Deliverables gets Priority/Complexity/Finished back on its own RD table (not Live board's, per 1.0.10's rationale) plus two new columns, Estimate and Actual, sourced from a new gate-records estimate_variance field: hooks/compute-estimate-variance.sh (new) runs automatically at commands/cz-gate.md step 8 on every 'approved' decision, comparing rd/*.md's estimate.expected_h/.pessimistic against the RD's actual build time computed purely from existing telemetry/events.jsonl timestamps for that rd id. Reports both actual_h (raw wall-clock span) and active_h (idle/blocked gaps over LOCK_TTL_S excluded); variance_pct and within_pessimistic_bound are computed against active_h, not actual_h, since an RD estimate is a work-effort guess, not a promise about time spent queued behind max_in_flight or waiting on a human gate. No token estimate/actual: Claude Code hooks have no real per-RD token/cost source (see hooks/emit-telemetry.sh's existing cost_usd comment for the same conclusion) — schemas/gate-record.schema.json documents estimate_variance's fields as an honest reflection of what's actually computed, nothing fabricated. agents/agentops.md's WEEKLY rollup responsibility now includes aggregating variance_pct across a period's accepted RDs to report systematic estimation bias. Verified against a real project's data via temporary symlinks (removed after) before commit; hooks/tests/*.sh suite unaffected (no existing hook's behavior changed).

1.0.10: correction to 1.0.9 — board/board.html's Live board table reverted to its original 6 columns (RD/Module/State/Agent/Time in state/Summary), no Priority/Complexity/Finished columns or priority filter. Rationale: this plugin's shared board.html has no "Deliverables" tab (that concept only exists in at least one downstream project's independently-forked board.html, which has a per-RD Deliverables table alongside its Live board); the user wants the three new columns on a Deliverables-style table, not the generic Live board, and this plugin doesn't ship one to put them on. schemas/rd.schema.json, templates/rd-template.yaml, hooks/project-state.sh, and schemas/board-state.schema.json are UNCHANGED from 1.0.9 — priority/complexity/finished_date remain real state/board.json fields (priority optional/defaults to "medium", complexity/finished_date computed by project-state.sh) available for any downstream project's own board rendering to consume, this plugin's stock board.html just doesn't render them.

1.0.9: user-requested board feature (not an audit finding) — RD table gained Priority, Complexity, and Finished columns. rd.schema.json/rd-template.yaml gained an optional `priority: low|medium|high` field (docs/TRACEABILITY.md and skills/traceability/SKILL.md already named `priority` as content_hash-excluded operational metadata, but it was never actually added to the schema/template until now); hooks/project-state.sh defaults it to "medium" for any RD without the field, so none of a project's existing rd/*.md files need a backfill. Complexity is display-only, not a stored field: project-state.sh buckets the RD's existing estimate.expected_h (already 0-4h) into low (<=1.5h) / medium (<=3h) / high (>3h). Finished date reuses gate-records/<id>-gate.json's gate_decision.timestamp, already read by project-state.sh for accepted-state time_in_state_s but previously discarded afterward — now also exposed as finished_date (null until accepted). board-state.schema.json documents all three new rds[] fields; board.html adds the two new columns plus a static low/medium/high priority filter (module/state filters stay dynamically populated since those value sets are open-ended; priority's is a fixed enum).

1.0.8: closed all 5 remaining Minor audit findings (N2-N5; N1 is a deliberate WONT-FIX, both extra commands kept by user decision) plus one incidentally-discovered bug: gates.yaml's module_overrides example now has an inert-by-design comment (N2); risk-gov.md's 'L0-L5' corrected to 'L0-L4' and cz-risk.md's invented A/B/C leash scale replaced with the real A/A+ vocabulary used everywhere else, including two incidental 'leash B' references in cz-viva.md/viva-prep/SKILL.md (N3); LIGHTWEIGHT-MODE.md's dangling /cz:trace reference fixed to the real command after a full-plugin sweep for other dangling command references found none (N4); gate-record.schema.json rewritten as a oneOf over the 3 real shapes actually used in production (flat phase-level, flat RD-level DOR, nested RD-level review-gate), mechanically validated against all 26 real gate-records/*.json files with 0 failures (N5). Separately: commands/cz-gate.md, skills/gate-engine/SKILL.md, and docs/OPERATOR-GUIDE.md had the gate-2 security-review trigger backwards ('leash=A' instead of 'leash=A+') — found and fixed alongside N3's related cz-risk.md fix; full-plugin grep confirms no remaining instances of the reversed condition. Full hooks/tests/*.sh suite (8 scripts, 73 assertions) re-run after every fix in this round — all pass, no regressions.

1.0.7: full audit pass against Plugin/CZ-HARNESS-PLAN-v0.4.md (see Plugin/CZ-HARNESS-AUDIT-2026-07-29.md for complete findings/fix log). All 9 Critical and 7 Major findings fixed and functionally verified (hooks/tests/*.sh — 8 scripts, 73 assertions, all pass): guard-secrets.sh's grep flag-misparse fail-open on private keys (C2); detect-hazard.sh's BSD-sed bug that silently disabled ALL hazard-path escalation (C1); cz-rd.md auto-committing RD splits with no human step by default (C3); guard-rd-freeze.sh's TC-staleness check being dead code against a sidecar mechanism nothing wrote (C4); contaminated state/telemetry/rd/ shipped inside the plugin package plus the CZ_ROOT-silently-falls-back-to-pwd root cause, now fails loudly instead (C5); guard-red-before-green.sh's cwd-relative red-log path bug, same root cause (M1); rd/*.yaml vs rd/*.md drift across 4 agents' tool grants plus 8 more files found in a full sweep (M2); the entirely-missing skills/ directory, now 7 real skills (C6); telemetry events not conforming to their own schema, reconciled at both the schema and emitter layer (C7); board cost_usd rollup, honestly null until a real cost source exists (C8); OPERATOR-GUIDE.md describing a fictional command/state set, rewritten from the real hook/command source (C9); the board-projection-from-telemetry-alone claim corrected to describe the real hybrid design (M5); board.html's missing leash badge and draft strip row (M6); agentops's append-only guarantee, now a byte-prefix hook check instead of prose (M3); outer-pipeline step ordering, now a real hook instead of prompt-only (M4); RD-GUIDE.md's non-schema-valid estimate/ac field names (M7). Five Minor items remain open (see audit file N1-N5). A pre-fix snapshot is kept at Plugin/_backups/cz-harness-1.0.5-phase0-pre-audit-fixes/.
This plugin defines the CONTRACTS (schemas, config, hook scripts, agent/command definitions, board) for CZ-Harness.

Per-project runtime state (rd/*.md — Markdown with a YAML frontmatter block, not bare *.yaml — tests/**, evidence/, gate-records/, deliverables/, telemetry/events.jsonl, state/) lives in the PROJECT repo that installs this plugin, not in the plugin itself.

deliverables/ is where every agent's narrative output lives (SCOPE/SPEC/ARCH/RISK/reviews/RTM/WEEKLY/CASE-STUDY/...), each auto-rendered to HTML via hooks/render-deliverable.sh using templates/deliverables/style.css + page.html.tmpl. See docs/DELIVERABLES.md.
Test runner target for the red/green hooks: pytest (decision recorded 2026-07-27). Other runners are adapters — see hooks/lib/test-runner-adapter.sh.

Open questions from plan §14 not yet resolved: FPT RD-template alignment (Q3), project-code convention for real projects (Q4), language (Q5). Treat rd-template.yaml as provisional until Q3 is answered.

1.0.3: UNDERSTANDING-LOG.md split into deliverables/understanding-log/<phase>.md + deliverables/understanding-log/rd/<rd-id>.md fragments (one writer per file) after a real incident where two RDs' concurrent /cz:dor reviews raced on the single shared file and lost its prior history to a last-write-wins overwrite. UL-<nnn> numbering is now fragment-local. See templates/UNDERSTANDING-LOG.md's header comment and docs/DELIVERABLES.md.

1.0.4: hooks/lib/common.sh gained a CZ_ACTING_AGENT/CZ_ACTIVE_RD 'Identity fallback' section (cz_sole_lock_agent/cz_sole_lock_rd/cz_lock_agent_for_rd/cz_extract_rd_id) since no command/agent runtime actually propagates those env vars across separate tool calls or into Task-dispatched subagents — hooks now resolve identity from state/locks/*.lock instead. guard-red-before-green.sh and guard-rd-freeze.sh were also reordered to try the active claim lock BEFORE grepping the target file's own RD-ID annotations, since a shared file (one file per module) carrying several RDs' annotations previously always resolved to whichever RD's annotation appeared first in the file, not the one actually being worked on — this was caught live when RD-AIBOOTCAMP-005.01a's build shared src/task-model.mjs with the already-green RD-AIBOOTCAMP-002.01a.

1.0.6: skills/ was listed in plan §11's repository layout (7 named skills: rd-decomposition, sdd-loop, gate-engine, traceability, telemetry, devbook, viva-prep) but the directory never existed and plugin.json had no skills field — audit finding C6. Added skills/<name>/SKILL.md for all 7, each self-sufficient (frontmatter description + substantive body pulled from the existing docs/*.md, commands/cz-*.md, plan sections, and config/schema/template files that already define the same territory, not new mechanics), and wired "skills": "./skills" here. Purely additive — no command, hook, agent, or config file changed.

1.0.5: nothing in the harness ever chained one command to the next — agents/sub-pm.md's frontmatter had no Task tool, so the agent documented as 'handing off' to ba/sa/planner/risk-gov/dev/test-designer/ai-reviewer/sec-reviewer/agentops could only compute what should happen next and write state/, leaving a human to invoke every slash command and every RD's /cz:dor -> /cz:build -> /cz:gate cycle by hand (setting human_gates.<phase> to false only removed the pause INSIDE an already-running command; it was never the thing that chained them). sub-pm now has Task and dispatches per its own handoff table, under a new hard rule 6 stating that dispatching is scheduling and never approving — hard rules 1-5 (no src/**, no gate approval, no gates.yaml edit, no committed RD split, hand off when in doubt) are unchanged. New commands/cz-run.md sequences those calls unattended and stops automatically on a true human_gates.<key> (treating an absent human_gates.scope as true — gates.yaml's last unconditional checkpoint), a hard-stop, budgets.per_wave_usd_hard, or exhaustion, reporting the blocking unit and the next manual action; it writes no gate record, flips no gate, and bypasses no hook. Purely additive — no existing command, hook, or one_way_ratchet invariant changed. See docs/OPERATOR-GUIDE.md §3a.
